description: Municipal and self-government (VÚC, mestá/obce) contracting authorities buying payment/cash solutions were not enumerated; only national-level buyers were mapped.
No CPV code set has been fixed for this cell yet; keyword-only searching in Slovak is noisy ('terminál', 'karta', 'pošta' all have high false-positive rates).
Bulk/structured access paths (ÚVO XML dumps on data.gov.sk, CRZ exports, TED API) were identified but their current schemas, endpoints and update cadence were not validated.
No SK procurement-review/appeal decision source was captured (ÚVO revízne postupy / rozhodnutia), which typically names losing bidders and disputed technical requirements.

Only Bratislava region/city and Košice were sampled from the sub-national layer; the other seven VÚC (Trnavský, Trenčiansky, Nitriansky, Žilinský, Banskobystrický, Prešovský, Košický) and the larger regional cities have their own registers or platform deployments that were not enumerated.

State-linked buyers highly relevant to payments were not yet resolved to their CRZ entity pages: Slovenská pošta's subsidiaries, DataCentrum (MF SR IT), Sociálna poisťovňa, Finančná správa SR (eKasa / cash-register infrastructure), Železničná spoločnosť Slovensko and municipal transport companies (ticketing terminals, card acceptance).

All discovery so far is buyer-side. The complementary vendor-side sweep — searching CRZ by the IČO of known payment/ATM/banking-IT suppliers active in SK — has not been run, and no vendor IČO list exists for this cell yet.
No assessment yet of what proportion of banking/payments contracts are attached as scanned images rather than text PDFs, which determines whether unit prices and SLAs can be extracted without OCR.

The link from a published contract back to its originating tender (or to the absence of one, i.e. a direct award) was identified as available via uvostat but not tested; the UVO/ÚVO procurement side belongs to a neighbouring cell and the join key was not established.

Dodatky (annexes) that change price, scope or extend term are the most commercially informative documents, but only Košice's portal was observed to explicitly link a contract to its amendment chain; how to reconstruct these chains in CRZ was not determined.

Diacritic-insensitive and inflected search behaviour of the CRZ search form was not tested (e.g. 'platobny' vs 'platobný', 'bankomatov' vs 'bankomat', 'terminálov'), nor whether it matches inside the contract text or only in metadata fields.
No agreed master watchlist of SK banking/payments vendor and competitor IČOs exists yet, so every register source here is currently unaddressable at scale.

The richest normalised views (FinStat Premium/ELITE/ULTIMATE, Foaf.sk connection depth, Slovensko.Digital premium API) are subscription-gated; free tiers give per-company profiles but not screening or bulk export.
International credit-bureau products for SK (e.g. Dun & Bradstreet / Bisnode-type, CRIF/Cribis) were not searched or documented in this cell.

Centrálny register zmlúv (crz.gov.sk) and the ÚVO tender/contract-award records — which reveal which entity actually signs and at what value — were only touched via ÚVO's operator register in this cell.
All URLs here come from search-result evidence; several deep endpoints (RÚZ API, RPO, ru.justice.sk JSF pages, ÚVO paths) were not fetched, and some are known to be session/CSRF dependent.

Member directories for ITAS, SAPIE, AmCham, Britcham, SLASPO, ALS SR, SASS, FINAS and SBCB/NBCB were identified but their full member rosters were not enumerated in this pass — only counts and sample names.

Employer/business umbrella bodies (Republiková únia zamestnávateľov, AZZZ SR, Klub 500, Slovenská obchodná a priemyselná komora) and the banking ombudsman were not searched in this cell; several banks and large IT firms sit on their bodies.

Associations of financial intermediaries and payment institutions (e.g. bodies representing finanční agenti / poskytovatelia platobných služieb) were not located; the intermediary channel is a distinct buyer of POS and onboarding technology.
Association conference/event sponsor lists — the strongest 'who sells into SK banking' signal in this cell — were not collected.

The URL for Slovenská kancelária poisťovateľov (skp.sk) was inferred rather than observed in results, and the ass.sk vs as3.sk distinction for asset-manager associations needs disambiguation (as3.sk is 'Asociácia správcov a správcovských spoločností', a different body concerning insolvency administrators).
Several event root domains (fintechroadmap.cz, amcham.sk event archive, the 'IT vo finančníctve' organiser) were inferred from press coverage rather than fetched directly.
Sponsor rosters are ephemeral — event sites routinely replace last year's partner wall with the current edition's, so multi-year sponsorship trend data is at risk.

LinkedIn event pages and company posts (Slovak Fintech Association, Qubit Conference, individual vendors) carry sponsorship and attendance announcements that never reach the event websites, but were not collected here.

CEE-wide events with SK participation (Prague/Vienna/Budapest payments and banking summits, Efma/Money20/20-style circuits) were only lightly probed via FinTech Roadmap; SK banks and their vendors are likely visible on those rosters too.
Visa-run SK awards, ATM/self-service and core-banking vendor user-group events, and any SBA/ZBK internal award were not located; only the Mastercard-run award was confirmed as a scheme award.
Agendas are frequently published as PDFs or in JS-rendered conference apps (program.itapa.sk), which plain HTML fetching will miss.

The three highest-value SK editorial sources for this cell (Trend, HNonline/Finweb, Dennik E) are all substantially paywalled, so automated full-text collection will capture only headlines and teasers.
No systematic way found to search historical SK trade-press archives (pre-2015) for banking IT projects; only oPeniazoch.sk showed deep paginated archive structure.

Trade-press coverage found here is skewed to the large retail banks (SLSP, Tatra banka, VUB, CSOB, 365.bank). Smaller/specialist institutions (Prima banka, Postova banka, PSS, Fio pobocka, Penta Bank, SZRB) and non-bank PSPs/acquirers surfaced only as directory entries.

Tender disputes and failed migrations — the cell's signature signal — were found for public-sector IT (UVO/slovensko.sk) but not for commercial bank procurement, which is private and not subject to public-procurement publicity.
Hungarian-language media serving southern Slovakia (e.g. ujszo.com) were not searched and may carry regional branch/ATM network coverage.

Career endpoints for SK-based system integrators and banking-software suppliers (Soitron, NESS KDC, DXC Slovakia, Asseco Central Europe, Accenture SK, IBM Slovensko, Monet+, Anasoft, Sygic-adjacent fintech suppliers) are not yet mapped.

Smaller and specialist SK institutions were not covered: Prima banka, Slovenska sporitelna leasing arms, Privatbanka, mBank SK branch, Tatra-Leasing, plus the state bank SZRB and the National Bank of Slovakia (NBS). NBS hiring for payment-system oversight and TIPS/instant-payment operations is an unexploited regulator-side signal.

No historical/archival route was established for expired job ads. Job ads are ephemeral (typically 30 days), so a collector started today has no back-history and cannot date a migration that began earlier.

The Slovak functional glossary needs hardening. Confirmed-productive terms so far: 'platobne systemy', 'kartove systemy', 'IT analytik', 'platobne riesenia'. Untested but likely: 'centralny bankovy system', 'jadrovy bankovy system', 'zuctovanie', 'autorizacia transakcii', 'bankomat' (ATM), 'akceptacia kariet', 'okamzite platby'/'instantne platby', 'migracia systemu', 'PSD2', 'AML system'. Slovak/Czech ads also mix English-in-Slovak tokens.

Specialist IT/finance recruitment agencies operating in SK (Hays, Grafton, Manpower, Talentwell and local boutiques) were identified only via a directory pointer, not individually. Agency ads are often the most technically explicit because the agency must screen on the platform.

Terms of service and robots.txt were not reviewed for Profesia.sk, kariera.zoznam.sk, join.titans.eu or the bank career sites; collection_allowed values in this slice are provisional assumptions of 'public site, ordinary terms apply'.
Petrol/fuel retail networks (Slovnaft, OMV SK, Shell, MOL) entirely uncovered for payment acceptance, self-service kiosks and cash handling.

Central Register of Contracts (CRZ, crz.gov.sk) and Register partnerov verejného sektora (RPVS) were not queried, although they hold signed contracts and beneficial ownership for public buyers (DPB, DPMK, Slovenská pošta, municipalities).
SK retail trade press (e.g. Tovar a Predaj, InStore Slovakia, retailmagazin.sk) not sampled; these are the likeliest place where self-checkout and POS suppliers are named.
Regional transport operators and the integrated systems beyond BA/KE (IDS BK, Žilina, Prešov, Banská Bystrica, SAD carriers, ZSSK rail ticketing) not scouted.
Every candidate here comes from search-result snippets; no URL liveness or content verification was performed, and one candidate (EMtest) has an inferred domain.
English-language coverage of this cell is thin — group-level Euronet/Loomis/Securitas investor and press material was not systematically searched.
The exact CPV code set relevant to SK banking/payments (ATM hardware, cash handling, card personalisation, core banking software, payment processing services, cash-in-transit) has not yet been fixed.
No verified list yet of SK contracting authorities in scope (NBS, state banks SZRB/Exportno-importná banka, Slovenská pošta, ministries and state IT bodies) that procure banking/payment technology.
The Slovak Central Register of Contracts (Centrálny register zmlúv) was not searched in this pass; it holds the actual signed contract texts behind awards, including annexes and prices.
SK e-procurement execution platforms (JOSEPHINE/proebiz, EVO/IS EVO, eZakazky, Tendernet) that host tender documentation referenced by ÚVO notices were not evaluated.
Commercial SK banks (Slovenská sporiteľňa, VÚB, Tatra banka, ČSOB, 365.bank) are not contracting authorities, so their vendor selections never appear in TED/ÚVO.
Whether EBRD ECEPP award notices for SK are visible without registration, and whether the EU Funding & Tenders SPA exposes a stable participant export, remain untested.

The list of licensed banks and foreign bank branches operating in SK was not separately captured in this cell; it sits in the subjekty.nbs.sk banking sector filter rather than in a distinct payments register.
EEA passporting inbound notifications — foreign PSPs and EMIs entitled to operate in Slovakia without a local licence — were not located as a discrete SK list in this pass.
The seed queries surfaced the reporting measure (opatrenie 11/2023) that defines card and terminal statistics, but not the actual published time-series in the NBS statistical data warehouse.

No regulator-side source in this cell names specific ICT/payments technology vendors serving SK institutions; the register-of-information data is confidential and licence-application annexes are not published.
Only the PSD2 API is confirmed machine-readable; the bulk 'Databáza na stiahnutie' export format on subjekty.nbs.sk was referenced but its format and stability were not confirmed.

Two SK-market banks disclose only through non-sk, non-en parent filings: UniCredit SK via Czech (výroční zpráva) and Italian group documents, mBank SK via Polish (raport roczny). The run's declared sk/en language scope cannot reach them.

No outsourcing register was located. Under EBA outsourcing guidelines and DORA, banks must maintain a register of outsourcing/ICT third-party arrangements and report critical ones to the supervisor — the single highest-value vendor-naming artefact in this cell. It was not found in public form for any SK bank.

Smaller and specialised SK banks in scope of the workstream were not covered in this pass: Slovenská záručná a rozvojová banka (SZRB), Privatbanka, J&T Banka SK, Fio banka SK, Oberbank SK, Komerční banka SK branch, Wüstenrot/PSS and ČSOB stavebná sporiteľňa. PSS's výročná správa did surface incidentally.

Vendor-side and integrator-side reference libraries were only spot-checked (one PosAm reference, one Temenos story). This proved to be the channel that actually yields names, yet no systematic list of Slovak banking IT integrators was compiled.

No URL in this slice was fetched and verified; all candidates come from search-result metadata. Several PDF URLs are long, deep-linked and version-suffixed (e.g. VÚB's '...AR_FS_VUB_2025_SK.pdf0', Prima banka's numeric preview-file ids) and are plausibly stale or malformed.

Disclosure cadence per bank was not established. Pillar 3 appears semi-annual at VÚB (period-coded filenames observed for 2024-06 and 2025-12) but the cadence for SLSP, Tatra banka, ČSOB, 365.bank and Prima banka is unconfirmed.
Newsrooms not yet located for mBank Slovensko, Oberbank SK, Slovenská záručná a rozvojová banka (SZRB), Eximbanka SR, ČSOB Poisťovňa, Generali Slovensko, Kooperativa (VIG), NN and Wüstenrot.
The Slovak glossary for biometric/remote onboarding and for wallet launches is incomplete, which produced a null result on a core cell topic.

State institutions beyond NBS, Slovenská pošta and MIRRI were not covered – notably Sociálna poisťovňa, Finančná správa SR, Ministerstvo financií SR, NASES/slovensko.sk and Úrad pre verejné obstarávanie.
Bank newsrooms prune older releases, so partnership announcements older than a few years may be unreachable at their original URLs.
Only two vendor-side mirrors (BLIK, Soitron) were captured, though the vendor half of an announcement is frequently more detailed than the bank half.
Country-filtered SK partner/reseller lists were not extracted from Verifone, Thales, Idemia, PAX, Ingenico/Worldline, Nexi or Oracle partner locators.
Finastra, Oracle Financial Services, PAX, Nexi and Temenos' own newsroom/client-stories sections were not individually crawled in this pass; only aggregate or third-party pages were reached.

The GDPR processor-list pattern that revealed Diebold Nixdorf at Slovenská sporiteľňa was only found for one bank; equivalent disclosures for VÚB, Tatra banka, ČSOB, Prima banka, 365.bank/Poštová banka, mBank, UniCredit Bank Slovakia and Slovenská záručná a rozvojová banka were not collected.

State-controlled or public-sector-adjacent banking bodies (NBS, Slovenská záručná a rozvojová banka, Exportno-importná banka SR) publish tenders and contracts that name vendors; this channel was not touched in this cell.
Vendor case studies carry no reliable publication dates in search snippets; the Temenos/Tatra banka item's currency and go-live status were not confirmed.
Beyond Printec Slovakia and Asseco CE, the SK integrator/reseller layer (local software houses reselling foreign core, card, fraud and POS platforms) is not enumerated.
No SK IT trade-press outlet was captured in this pass (e.g. itnews.sk, touchIT, PC REVUE, TREND) even though they carry the majority of SK integrator project announcements and interviews.
Primary Slovak procurement and contract registers (ÚVO/uvo.gov.sk, CRZ crz.gov.sk) were not directly captured; only the derived uvostat analytics were.

Job-board evidence (profesia.sk, bank and integrator career pages) was not collected, though it is the fastest indicator of which technologies SK banks and their hubs are staffing for and which integrators are ramping bank delivery teams.
Bank-owned service hubs other than Erste Digital (e.g. hubs of VÚB/Intesa, Tatra banka/Raiffeisen, ČSOB/KBC in SK) were not enumerated.
Industry event programmes (ITAPA and banking/fintech conferences) were not captured; speaker lists and agendas reveal integrator-bank pairings and named projects before any case study is published.

Bank-owned acquiring arms and their gateway brands (Tatra banka CardPay, VÚB eCard, ČSOB, 365.bank, Slovenská sporiteľňa) were only reached indirectly via comparison articles and one bank partner page; their own acceptance/pricing pages were not enumerated.

No public-procurement or tender source was scouted, although SK state and municipal bodies procure POS terminals, acquiring and payment gateways — a category that names vendors, volumes and prices explicitly.

A2A/instant-payments commercial actors beyond the scheme registers — VOP, Request-to-Pay, and open-banking PISP-based checkout in SK — were only touched via SKPAY and generic EPC material; Viamo was named but no primary source was located.
Card-scheme SK activity is currently sourced only through re-published PR; no Visa or Mastercard SK-market page, local interchange/fee disclosure, or SK licensee list was scouted.
All URLs in this slice are search-derived and none were fetched; several (NBS deep links, EPC register paths, worldline sk-SK deep paths) are long and prone to redirect or restructure.
The FINAS and Slovenská FinTech asociácia member rosters — the core deliverable of this cell — were located but not extracted.
Inbound EU passporting into SK is not covered by any located register. Wise, Curve and other e-money/payment passportees have no confirmed SK-facing source.
No Dealroom SK fintech slice and no StartupBlink/EU-Startups SK slice were captured, despite Dealroom being explicitly in scope.

Named SK funds surfaced only in passing (Crowdberry, Neulogy Ventures, Sandberg Investment Fund II, SeedStarter, Slovak Investment Holding; DEPO Ventures and Passion Capital as cross-border co-investors). None of their portfolio pages were visited.
The Slovak Investment Holding domain (sih.sk) was inferred from the entity name rather than confirmed by a fetch or a search result.
Bank-side partnership disclosures (SLSP, 365.bank, Tatra banka, VÚB innovation/press pages) were touched only incidentally via the SLSP–Crowdberry landing page and the SLSP-authored Startup Report.
